name: utf8
resume: All nine exports are done. Widths use the utf8lite table from utf8 1.2.6. The compiled code is C, so there is no crate. Python strings have no R encoding mark; bytes stand for a byte string.

functions.name: as_utf8
functions.done: Decodes UTF-8 bytes and, when asked, composes to NFC.

check.case: A plus a combining ring, composed

proof.python:
import io
import json
import statistics
import time

from utf8 import (
    as_utf8,
    output_ansi,
    output_utf8,
    utf8_encode,
    utf8_format,
    utf8_normalize,
    utf8_print,
    utf8_valid,
    utf8_width,
)
def one():
    return as_utf8("A\u030a", normalize=True)

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(json.dumps({"value": value, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}, ensure_ascii=False))

functions.name: utf8_valid
functions.done: A string is valid. bytes are valid when they decode as UTF-8.

check.case: façile and abc are valid UTF-8

import io
import json
import statistics
import time

    as_utf8,
